Data Model & Storage ​

Saidi keeps structured records in MongoDB and artifacts on disk. The split is deliberate: durable structured data lives in Mongo, while human-editable markdown memory and the scanned project registry stay as files because they are meant to be inspected and edited. Binary run output (images, deliverables, git worktrees) never enters the database.

Storage engine ​

MongoDB, accessed through Mongoose (mongoose@^9). There is no file-backed fallback: connectMongo() returns false on failure and the orchestrator treats that as fatal.

Mongo is the source of truth for every store. The connection is managed by the platform; nothing about it is configurable from a workspace.

BehaviourValue
Server selection timeout2500 ms on connect, 1500 ms for the pingMongo probe
Mongoose flagsstrictQuery: true, bufferCommands: false
On disconnectedLogs and exits after a 1 s grace window, so every in-memory working set is rebuilt from the DB on restart

Every collection below is scoped by orgId. A query that could span workspaces is a bug, not a feature — see Tenancy, Identity & Access.

External edits ​

Saidi opens a MongoDB change stream filtered to delete/drop/dropDatabase/invalidate on the runs and activity collections only — the application itself never deletes those, so any such event is an external edit (mongosh, Compass, a restored dump). Events are debounced 250 ms, then the affected store is resynced for every loaded org and clients are told to re-pull. Change streams require a replica set; on a standalone mongod the watcher disables itself with a warning and external edits only appear after a restart.

Collections ​

Nineteen models define these schemas. Every one uses versionKey: false and minimize: false. Records that own a globally unique string id store it as _id (runs, crons, reflexes, playbooks, users, orgs); records whose id is only unique within an org use a compound _id (<orgId>::<id> for chats and agent definitions, <orgId>:<rel> for memory); platform-global blobs live under a fixed id.

ActivityEvent ​

Append-only stream of operator directives, PRIME replies, tool steps and agent results.

FieldTypeMeaning
idString (indexed)The event's own id
tNumber (required, indexed)Epoch ms
orgIdString (indexed)Owning org; absent on legacy local rows
actor / msgString (required)Who spoke, and the line
detailStringFull tool call/output for the expandable row
channelString (indexed)main or run; legacy rows without it count as main

statssubdocumentinputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheCreationTokens, ms, contextTokens, costUsd, costShared, model

Three indexes back it: { orgId: 1, t: -1 } for the startup window, { orgId: 1, conversationId: 1, t: -1 } for opening one chat, and a plain text index on msg + detail for recall. The text index is deliberately not compound with orgId, because local rows carry no orgId at all and a prefixed index would exclude them.

AgentDef ​

One document per custom agent directory tree, per org.

FieldTypeMeaning
_idString (required)<orgId>::<name>
orgIdString (indexed)Owning workspace
nameString (required, indexed)The agent's own name
files[{ rel, b64 }] (default [])Every packed file: forward-slash path under the agent dir, plus its bytes base64-encoded
skipped[String] (default [])Paths left out of files because packing them would exceed MongoDB's 16 MB document limit — they exist on disk only and the materializer preserves them
updatedAtNumber (required)Newest mtime in the tree

Packing bounds the payload at 12 MB and takes files smallest-first, so AGENT.md, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, skills/*/SKILL.md and mcp.json always fit. mcp-auth/ (per-server OAuth tokens), workspace/ and any node_modules are never packed and never leave disk.

How runs are persisted ​

RunStore holds the in-memory working copy and delegates durability to a RunPersistence adapter. MongoRunPersistence is production; FileRunPersistence (<runsRoot>/<id>/run.json) is a unit-test adapter.

Writes come in two flavours. persist() is immediate and used for creation and every lifecycle or participant change, so a crash never loses a critical transition. persistSoon() coalesces the hot append path on a 750 ms debounce; an immediate write cancels any pending debounced flush because it is a superset of it.

Inside the Mongo adapter, persist() picks one of two paths:

  • Delta (append-only fast path). Taken when a per-run high-water mark exists, thread and usageLog only grew, and the previously written prefix is intact (checked by comparing the id of the last written event). It $pushes only the new tail, $sets the small scalar fields, and $unsets the cleared optional keys listed in CLEARABLE_RUN_KEYS so a removed pendingApproval or attention actually disappears.
  • Full replaceOne. Taken on the first write of a run in the process, or when the thread was rewound so the prefix no longer matches.

Two more details matter:

  • patchEvents() rewrites thread events edited in place, addressed by index. The delta path treats thread as append-only, so stamping a settled turn's cost back onto earlier messages is invisible to it. Only positions below the high-water mark are patched — $setting past the stored array's length would pad it with nulls.
  • Writes for one run are serialized through a per-id promise chain, because every write carries the full scalar set including status; two overlapping fire-and-forget writes could otherwise land out of order and revert a settled run to active. Different runs still write concurrently. flush() drains the chains (up to five passes) so shutdown completes before the connection drops.

Any failed write drops the high-water mark, which makes the next write a full replaceOne that self-heals.

How runs are reloaded ​

RunStore.init() loads durable records once at startup via loadAsync(). Each record goes through mergeLoaded():

  • An older durable copy never replaces a newer in-memory one (updatedAt wins).
  • A run left active or awaiting_input when the process stopped is downgraded to paused; the engine never auto-resumes. A SYSTEM thread event is appended naming each killed in-flight delegation (up to five), so the interruption is visible and PRIME's live-state block knows what died.
  • A resting run that still carries inFlight/inFlights has them cleared.

RunStore.reload() is the out-of-band resync. It fetches the newest 500 runs by updatedAt (RELOAD_LIMIT) so a large org never pulls every full run document. Because the fetch is bounded, "absent from the list" no longer means "deleted": an in-memory run is only evicted if it is absent and its updatedAt is at or above the oldest fetched run. With protectActive, live runs are left alone — their newest streamed events may not be persisted yet. A durable copy older than the in-memory one is never applied.

See Runs for the lifecycle these rules protect.

Where files live ​

Alongside Mongo, each workspace has a file tree that agents actually read and write. It is nested one level per workspace, and no user-supplied id is ever joined into a path, so nothing can escape its own workspace root.

orgs/<orgId>/
├── memory/
│   ├── members/<userId>/global.md      # per-member personal memory
│   ├── members/<userId>/learning.json
│   ├── learning.json                   # structured learned memory sidecar
│   ├── projects/<name>.md              # per-project memory, shared across the workspace
│   ├── agents/<name>.md                # per-agent memory, shared across the workspace
│   ├── chat/log.json                   # main-chat agent call log
│   ├── chat-uploads/                   # files attached to main-chat messages
│   ├── activity-log.json               # activity window fallback when Mongo is down
│   ├── activity-unsynced.jsonl         # journal of activity not yet in Mongo
│   └── runs/<runId>/                   # see below
├── agents/                             # custom agent definition dirs
│   └── <name>/AGENT.md, skills/<slug>/SKILL.md, mcp.json,
│       .claude-plugin/plugin.json, mcp-auth/, workspace/
├── config/
└── repos/                              # per-workspace repo checkouts

Each run owns a directory under the org's runs/ root :

Path helperDirectoryPurpose
runDir(id)runs/<id>The run's whole on-disk folder
runAssetsDir(id)runs/<id>/assetsImages and deliverables served via /api/run-asset
runWorkRoot(id)runs/<id>/workMounted as /workspace in the run's sandbox
runWorkDir(id, agent)runs/<id>/work/<agent>One agent's per-run workspace
runRepoRoot(id) / runRepoDir(id, project)runs/<id>/repos[/<project>]Private git worktrees, kept outside the repo so they never show up as untracked files in a diff
runOutputDir(id)runs/<id>/outputSandbox drop zone (/run/output), swept into assets after each delegation
runSharedDir(id)runs/<id>/sharedCross-agent handoff notes (/run/shared)
runConfigRoot(id)runs/<id>/agent-configPer-run SDK config/session store, so resume transcripts survive across delegations
—runs/<id>/log.jsonThe run's agent call log

promoteRunAssets() copies (never moves) generated files from the run-level output/ drop zone and each agent workspace's assets/ and output/ subdirectories into the served assets dir, skipping names that already exist and ignoring up- prefixed uploads. Files must match ^[\w.-]+$ to be listed.

Deleting a run removes the Mongo document and, unless you keep files, the whole runs/<id>/ directory — the record and the artifacts are separate deletions because assets live on disk in every mode.

Materialized working copies ​

Two things exist in both places, with Mongo authoritative:

  • Memory. initOrgMemory(orgId) runs on org hydration: it deletes on-disk files whose documents are gone, then writes every document's content to its rel path. persistMemory(rel, content) and syncMemoryFileToMongo(full) write changes back. All writes are best-effort and fire-and-forget — memory must never break a turn — and no-op when Mongo is down. Only the enumerated paths are synced (global.md, learning.json, members/<id>/*, projects/*.md, agents/*.md), so a generated file such as INDEX.md at the memory root is never touched.
  • Agent definitions. initAgents() re-materializes an org's agent directories from Mongo on first access, and every mutation mirrors back. Stored rel paths are validated against the agent root and the agent name against ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,40}$ so a poisoned document cannot write outside the org's agents dir.

Legacy per-store JSON files (crons.json, chats.json, reflexes.json, playbooks.json, credits.json, credit-ledger.jsonl, secrets.json) are migration input only. In production every store is constructed with loadLegacyFile: false, so it neither reads nor rewrites them.
